reviews.decision: Keep the CUDA resource adapter together; the signals cover allocation and stream lifecycle coordination.
Keep host/device fallback orchestration in the HIP boundary; kernel launch contracts are now separate records.
Keep KDK transaction ordering in one integration contract; the branches are rollback and finite-state gates.
Keep Morton partitioning and ownership validation together because they share the decomposition invariant.
Keep scalar and status collective validation together; the branches protect one opaque MPI contract for root distribution and bounded exchanges.
Keep MPI capability and collective adapters behind one opaque context boundary.
Keep process-level MPI ownership and shutdown policy together; the branches guard initialization, external ownership, and process-exit finalization.
Keep packet migration and gather validation together; the long paths are bounded transport state machines.
Keep non-blocking halo packing and completion in one responsibility; buffers are prepared before execution.
Keep wire-format validation, dynamic capacity growth, and MPI packet transfer together because they protect one bounded packet contract.
Keep the two bounded buffer facades together; their shared ownership and span contract are intentionally symmetric.
Keep the C ABI translation layer together; exported V1 shims and V2 validation are one ABI boundary.
Keep the move-only C++ facade adapters together; they are thin ownership-preserving calls into the C ABI.
The facade owns solver and runtime composition, so its dependency set is intentional and remains private to the SDK.
Keep CPU, HIP fallback, distributed dispatch, and fixed-size overlap qualification in the dispatch responsibility; the added timeline state does not own transport or solver resources.
Keep state staging and commit validation together; they publish the same arena ownership transition.
Keep distributed step transaction, migration, and post-migration solver preparation together; they form one atomic KDK state transition.
Keep particle input commit and output gather together because both define the SDK to arena state boundary.
Keep tree construction and force traversal together; the long path is the solver algorithm, not a mixed service object.
Keep reference-force validation and bounded staging together because they define the ground-truth solver contract.
Keep the device traversal in one kernel source; launch parameters are isolated in a bounded request record.
Keep tiled direct accumulation in one kernel source; the host launch contract is now a single validated request.
Keep octree build, validation, and traversal support together because they share cell/index ownership invariants.
